attempted_claim: Let S be the once-punctured genus-two surface S_{2,1}. Consider the set R of positive (cusped Hitchin) representations rho: pi1(S)->PSL(3,R) with unipotent peripheral holonomy, in Fock-Goncharov coordinates on a fixed ideal triangulation (all edge cross-ratios >0 and all triangle invariants >0), with Labourie cross-ratios from the Frenet curve. Fix a disjoint nonseparating cuff pair (p,q) cutting off a one-holed torus subsurface, e.g. p=[a1,b1] commutator-side curve and q=a2 standard generator disjoint from p. For loxodromic g write simple-root lengths l1(g)=log|lambda1/lambda2|, l2(g)=log|lambda2/lambda3| and gap D_rho(g)=l1(g)-l2(g) (eigenvalue-ratio asymmetry, zero exactly on the Fuchsian locus). Decide the gap-coherence inequality: is D_rho(p)*D_rho(q) >= 0 for every rho in R, i.e. the two fixed cuffs always bulge to the same side of the Fuchsian locus, decidable via Fock-Goncharov shear/triangle formulas for the two monodromy matrices plus cross-ratio identities? Scope is the full positive locus with unipotent puncture. A complete answer is either a rigorous proof of nonnegativity for all rho in R, or one explicit positive coordinate tuple with rigorously diagonalized rho(p),rho(q) whose computed gaps have strictly opposite nonzero signs.
